title: Adaptive latency-slice admission with progressive decode truncation and tenant stability profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a new load-shedding primitive that assigns a per-request latency slice and enforces it via admission checks, ranked priority queues, and progressive decode truncation. The feature introduces tenant stability profiles so we avoid oscillating quality for high-value customers, and a shadow-validation pipeline that assesses degraded output quality without affecting production traffic. The goal is to reduce SLO breach rate during transient overloads while keeping end-user quality loss bounded and measurable.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side: new admission layer accepts a 'latency_slice_ms' token on request context and enforces per-request execution budget with preemptive trimming
Priority queues: implementation supports 3 soft priority bands (critical, default, best-effort) with configurable weighting and fair decay for long tails
Degradation modes: support progressive truncation (truncate decode after N tokens), prefix-only response, cached-summary fallback, and lightweight model fallback
Tenant stability profiles: profiles can pin a tenant to 'stability' or 'opportunistic' and are respected by admission and trimming logic
Shadow validation: degraded outputs are routed to asynchronous validators that compute quality deltas and push metrics to the console without adding latency to the real response
SLO alignment: platform telemetry shows reduced 99th percentile latency SLO breaches under synthetic overload by >= 50% in canary
Observability: per-tenant SLO burn, average quality delta, fallback rates, and circuit-breaker trips are visible in per-route dashboards
Runbook: oncall runbook updated with steps for circuit-breaker resets, manual tenant pinning, and rollout rollback
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spec drafted with initial API proposals for 'latency_slice_ms' and 'stability_profile' flags; reviewed with reliability team; feedback: add explicit validity window for slices.
2026-03-05: Prototype admission middleware implemented in runtime edge; basic priority queue integration working against local loadgen; observed stable p50 but p99 still spikes at high QPS.

2026-03-08: Added progressive decode truncation: runtime can abort decoding early and return partial structured output. Hooked up a lightweight fallback path to cached summaries for large generation requests.
2026-03-10: Tenant stability profiles implemented, defaulting to 'opportunistic'. Verified that high-value tenant pinned to 'stability' avoids automatic truncation under test load.

2026-03-12: Shadow validation pipeline MVP live on canary cluster; collects ROUGE/BLEU-like metrics and a small human-eval sampler. Initial quality delta for truncated responses ~7% drop on summary tasks.
2026-03-14: Observability dashboards added (route-level fallback rates, per-tenant stability pins, circuit-breaker state machine). Preparing canary against production traffic fraction next week.
review_feedback: PM (Evelyn Gomez): Ensure we expose safe defaults; avoid surprise quality regressions for free-tier customers. Suggest adding opt-out header per-tenant.
Design (Diego Ramirez): Present partial responses clearly in client SDKs; we need a structured 'degraded' envelope so clients can render a subtle notice.
Security (Priya Nair): Shadow validation must redact any PII before storing; added requirement to use KMS for validator artifacts retention.
notes_for_oncall: If circuit-breaker trips for a region: 1) failover to secondary region per multi-region policy, 2) temporarily increase 'latency_slice_ms' for critical priority to avoid long tail aborts, 3) pin large-paying tenants to 'stability' until root-cause resolved. Documented in runbook link.
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission logic + property tests for fairness decay; e2e stress test with workload generator that simulates multi-region latency spikes; human-in-the-loop quality sampling for truncated responses; canary at 1% traffic with 24h observation before 5% ramp.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal QA cluster smoke, 2) Canary 1% traffic (2 regions) for 48h, observe SLO and quality metrics, 3) Ramp to 10% after thresholds met, 4) Full rollout with scheduled Ops window. Rollback: toggle feature-by-tenant or disable admission layer via infra flag.
risks: Potential client misinterpretation of partial responses; slight cost increase due to shadow validation; complexity added to admission logic could introduce regressions in p50 under pathological workloads.
mitigations: SDK changes to expose 'degraded' envelope; cap shadow validation sampling to 5% for first month; thorough canary with synthetic overloads and chaos testing for decoder aborts.
